texts.facts: formal charges in terms of order dated 06.08.2020 were framed against revisionist on 11.03.2022. 2. The facts as noted by Ld. Trial Court are being reproduced for the sake of convenience as under :- "Briefly stated the case of prosecution is that, it is stated that the mother of complainant Naresh Kumar Pandey became the owner of property No. 104/5, Ring Road, Maharani Bagh, New Delhi on 19.08.1912 and that on 17.05.1993, the mother of complainant availed a packing credit facility from Bank of Madura in favour of one of her son's firm 'Mega Marketing' for Rs. 10 lakhs and mortgaged the said property by way of depositing of title deeds of the said property on 18.05.1993. It is alleged that the mother of the complainant also executed a letter of guarantee on 17.05.1993 Om Dutt Sharma vs State (Nct Of Delhi) on 9 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142400357/ 1 and that on 26.06.1993,. As per the chargesheet, the mother of complainant passed away leaving behind seven legal heirs to the property including the complainant. It is further alleged that the father of V.K. Jain, accused persons Sh. Saurabh Jain, Gaurav Jain and Manav Jain, who was a business associate of the brother of the complainant and used to frequently visit the house of the complainant, had requested the mother of the complainant Smt. Kanti Devi to allow the said property be used for two weeks on the ground that their Guruji was coming to Delhi for some days and believing on their representations, the mother of complainant allowed them to use the said property for two weeks. It is alleged that after the death of mother of the complainant, when her legal heirs told the accused persons to vacate the said property and hand over the possession to them, they were told by accused persons V.K. Jain, Gaurav Jain, Saurabh Jain, Manav Jain that their mother had sold the property to them for Rs.13.5 Lakhs on 23.05.1993 and they produced a receipt and Will of Late Smt. Kanti Devi of the same date purportedly issued by the mother of the complainant and refused to hand over the said property to the complainant and his family. It is also alleged that the accused persons by using the forged documents had even managed to get meter connection on the said property. Crl Rev. No. 149/2021 Om Dutt Sharma Vs State (Govt of NCT Of Delhi) ANUJ ANUJ AG AGRAWAL Date: 2 14:19:1 It is further alleged that during investigation it was revealed that another person namely, Sh. T.R. Anand, Director, Royal Towers Pvt. Ltd. had filed a suit against the legal heirs of the deceased mother of the complainant for restraining them for dispossessing of the said property being suit no. 65/94 pending before Ld. Civil Judge, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi and T.R. Anand had also denied that the mother of the complainant had sold the said property to him on 18.05.1993 for Rs. 57 Lakhs and that the accused persons had moved an application seeking to impleaded as a party in the suit filed by Sh. T.R. Anand and in support of their contentions they had filed forged receipt, Will and affidavits thereby purporting themselves to be legal heirs. It has been also submitted in the chargesheet that the accused persons had even mutated the said property in their names with active connivance of the concerned officials. Further, as per the chargesheet, the mother of the complainant had deposited the title deed of the said bank with the Bank of Madura, when Packing Facility Loan was availed and that till the filing of the chargesheet, the same were Om Dutt Sharma vs State (Nct Of Delhi) on 9 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142400357/ 2 lying with the Bank of Madura against the legal heirs for recovery of the loan amount. During investigation, it was also found that the Will and the receipt produced by the alleged persons also bore the signatures as witnesses of Sh. S.C. Pandey, Sh. K.C. Pandey and accused Sh. Rajesh Kumar Pandey. Further, the Notary Sh. Surender Kumar has also stated during investigation that he had notoraized the documents on the request of Sh. K.C. Pandey and accused Rajesh Pandey. Also, as per the FSL report, it was confirmed that the signatures of the Will and Receipts as witnesses were executed by accused Rajesh Pandey and K.C. Pandey. Further, as per the chargesheet and FSL Report the impugned Will and the receipt did not contain the signatures of Smt. Kanti Devi and the same were forged. Further, it has been mentioned in the chargesheet that the independent witness namely Sh. S.C. Pandey, who is a distant relative of legal heirs had stated during interrogation that he had signed the documents at the behest of Sh. K.C. Pandey and accused Rajesh Pandey. It is also stated in the chargesheet that during investigation Crl Rev. No. 149/2021 Om Dutt Sharma Vs State (Govt of NCT Of Delhi) Page No. 3 of 12 ANUJ ANUJ AGRAWAL AGRAWAL Date: 2023.05.09 14:19:21 +0530 with respect to the restoration of the file in favour of the accused persons, the original file of MCD was seized and it was found that original NOC forms were not in the file but only photocopies were found and that on scrutiny of MCD file, it was revealed that Naresh Pandey had lodged a complaint with MCD authorities that the mutation of the property should not be done in the name of Gaurav Jain, Saurabh Jain and Manav Jain, as the documents contained the forged signature of mother, Smt. Kanti Devi and despite the observation by the concerned official on the matter seeking further examination of accused Om Dutt Sharma, Zonal Inspector and MMS Bhatnagar, Sr. assessor and collector, mutated the property in favour of accused persons after their predecessors were transferred. It is alleged in the chargesheet that accused persons hatched a criminal conspiracy in collusion with each other and committed the offences of cheating, forgery, house trespass and causing disappearance of evidence pursuant to their common intention." 3. Trial Court record reveals that Ld. CMM after considering the arguments advanced on behalf of prosecution as well as defence and on the basis of material available on record passed the impugned order dated 06.08.2020 inter-alia observing as under :- "Qua accused Om Dutt Sharma, it is seen that mutation of property was done in the name of accused persons Saurabh Jain, Gaurav Jain and Manav Jain by the MCD record by forging signatures of the legal heirs on their request. Further, only the photocopy of NOC were found available in the files of MCD which were seized and mutation was allowed on photocopy by accused Om Dutt Sharma, Zonal Inspector and Ms Bhatnagar, Joint Assessor and Collector pursuant to the criminal conspiracy. Om Dutt Sharma vs State (Nct Of Delhi) on 9 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142400357/ 3 It is further alleged as per chargesheet that accused Om Dutt Sharma pursuant to the criminal conspiracy had purposely removed the original NOC forms and mutated the property in favour of other co-accused persons after his then predecessors retired................" 3A.
texts.arguments: 4. Aggrieved with the said order of Ld CMM, revisionist Om Dutt Sharma has preferred the present revision petition seeking setting aside of impugned order and prays for his discharge. The sum and substance of arguments of Ld. Counsel revisionist are as under:- (i) That the impugned order is bad in law, resulting in grave miscarriage of justice; (ii) That Ld Trial court has failed to appreciate that in the FIR No. 422/2001 under revision, there are no allegations against the revisionist in particular except the bald allegations some officials of MCD were involved and facilitated the accused persons; (iii) That Ld. Trial Court failed to appreaciate that the limited role of revisionist is that he was Zonal Inspector In-charge at the time when mutation was allowed and he had merely submitted report to A & C Deptt., MCD and calculated tax; (iv) That Ld Trial court failed to consider that the revisionist cannot be held liable for fraud/forgery, if any, committed by accused persons who themselves gave undertaking in form of indemnity bond to MCD, if the title is found defective; (v) That Ld Trial Court failed to appreciate that Ld. ASJ vide order dated 08.08.2003 while granting bail to the revisionist opined that no offence is made out against revisionist and if mutation is wrongly granted, MCD is open to cancel it; (vi) That the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that the respondent no. 2 did not challenge the Will, possession of other accused persons and order dated 24.09.1998 of MCD Tribunal which became final, whereby appeal was allowed and it was held that there appears no defect in title of other accused persons and defect, if any, found can be rectified by MCD by revoking building plans; (vii) That Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that application for mutation was submitted the accused persons on 21.04.1994 i.e. prior to the joining of the revisionist in A & C Deptt, MCD on Crl Rev. No. 149/2021 Om Dutt Sharma Vs State (Govt of NCT Of Delhi) Page No . 5 of 12 4A. Ld. Counsel for revisionist has relied upon following judgments in support of his contentions :- a) R.R.Gautam and Anr. vs. State and Anr. 2008(1) JCC 766; b) Union of India vs. Prafulla Kumar Samal & Anr. AIR 1979 SC 366; c) State of Karnatka s. L. Muniswamy, AIR 1977 SC 1489; d) State of Bihar vs. Ramesh Singh, AIR 1977 SC 2018; e) State of M.P. s. S.B. Johari, 2000 Crl. L.J 944 (SC); f) P.Vijayan vs. State of Kerala 2010 Crl. L.J. 1427; 5. Per contra, Ld. Addl PP for State/ respondent vehemently argued that there is no infirmity in the impugned order as the same was passed after considering all the material available on record and keeping in view the facts and circumstances of the present case. It was further argued that the revisionist being Zonal Inspector in criminal conspiracy with other co-accused allowed mutation on photocopy. It was argued that pursuant to the criminal conspiracy, revisionist purposely removed original NOC Forms and mutated the property in favour of co-accused persons after his predecessors retired. It was further argued that firstly revisionist cannot claim protection u/s 197 CrPC as he was removable from his office by MCD and not by Central or State Government. It was submitted that the present revision petition is misconceived and therefore same is liable to be dismissed. 7. As to the issue whether revisionist enjoys protection u/s 197 CrPC, it is settled law that said protection is not available to an official like revisionist. Reliance is placed upon judgment Hon'ble Apex Court in Lakshmansingh Himatsingh vs. Naresh Kumar Chandrashankar Jha, AIR 1990 SC 1976, wherein it was held as under:- Om Dutt Sharma vs State (Nct Of Delhi) on 9 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142400357/ 5 "Section 197, Cr.P.C., clearly intends to draw a line between public servants and to provide that only in the case of the higher ranks should the sanction of the government to their prosecution be necessary. While a public servant holding an office of the kind mentioned in the Section is as such public servant appointed to another office, his official acts in connection with the latter office will also relate to the former office. The words "removable from office" occurring in Section 197 signify removal from the office he is holding. The authority mentioned in the section is the authority under which the officer is serving and competent to terminate his services. The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act also does not contain any deeming provision to treat the Public Analyst as a Crl Rev. No. 149/2021 Om Dutt Sharma Vs State (Govt of NCT Of Delhi) Page No. 7 of 12 ANUJ 16. Hon'ble Apex Court in the matter of Union of India vs. Prafulla Kumar Samal and Ors., AIR 1979 SC 366, has held that the Court has the power to sift and weigh the evidence for the limited purpose of finding out whether a prima facie case against the accused is made out or not. It has been further held that where the material placed before the Court disclosed a grave suspicion against the accused, which has not been properly explained, the Court will be fully justified in framing a charge and proceeding with the trial. By and large, however, if two views are Crl Rev. No. 149/2021 Om Dutt Sharma Vs State (Govt of NCT Of Delhi) Page No. 10 of 12 ANUJ ANUJ AGRAWAL AGRAWAL Date: 2023.05.09 14:20:59 +0530 equally possible and the Judge is satisfied that the evidence produced before him gives rise to some suspicion, but not grave suspicion against the accused, he will be fully within his right to discharge the accused. It is a settled law that the presumption howsoever strong cannot take place of proof. Relevant portion of the afore-mentioned judgment is reproduced hereinunder: "10. Thus, on a consideration of the authorities mentioned above, the following principles emerge: (1) That the Judge while considering the question of framing the charges under Section 227 of the Code has the undoubted power to sift and weigh the evidence for the limited purpose of finding out whether or not a prima facie case against the accused has been made out: (2) Where the materials placed before the Court disclose grave suspicion against the accused which has not been properly explained the Court will be fully justified in framing a charge and proceeding with the trial. (3) The test to determine a prima facie case would naturally depend upon the facts of each case and it is difficult to lay down a rule of universal application. By and large however if two views are equally possible and the Judge is satisfied that the evidence produced before him while giving rise to some suspicion but not grave suspicion against the accused, he will be fully within his right to discharge the accused. (4) That in exercising his jurisdiction under Section 227 of the Code the Judge which under the present Code is a senior and experienced Judge cannot act merely as a Post Office or a mouth- piece of the prosecution, but has to consider the broad probabilities of the case, the total effect of the evidence and the documents produced before the Court, any basic infirmities appearing in the case and so on. Om Dutt Sharma vs State (Nct Of Delhi) on 9 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142400357/ 8 17. If the present case is tested upon the touchstone of settled Crl Rev. No. 149/2021 Om Dutt Sharma Vs State (Govt of NCT Of Delhi) Page No. 11 of 12 ANUJ principles
